svg.text: Three-tier, multi-AZ, EC2-based reference architecture · Region eu-west-1 · all compute in private subnets, no SSH, no bastion
internet-facing · one node in each public subnet · listener HTTPS 443 → target group HTTP 80 · health check GET /health
Elastic IP · zonal, one per AZ
Elastic IP · zonal, one per AZ
min 2 · desired 2 · max 6 · target tracking 50% CPU
shell over an outbound tunnel · no inbound rule, no SSH key
chained by reference, never by CIDR
no port 22 rule anywhere in the VPC
End user resolves the apex record and connects over HTTPS 443.
Route 53 A-record alias points at the CloudFront distribution.
Static assets served from the edge cache, S3 origin on a miss.
Dynamic requests reach the ALB origin over HTTPS 443, uncached.
ALB forwards to a healthy target on HTTP 80, across both AZs.
Web tier queries the RDS writer endpoint on TCP 3306.
Synchronous replication to the standby; failover in 60–120 s.
Outbound traffic exits via the NAT gateway in its own AZ, then the IGW.
Administrators open a shell through Session Manager — no inbound rule.
Metrics, logs and alarms to CloudWatch; notifications via SNS.
